name: Cottagecore

media.title: Anne of Green Gables (1908 novel; multiple adaptations)
Studio Ghibli films (e.g. My Neighbor Totoro, Kiki's Delivery Service)
media.note: frequently cited visual references in cottagecore moodboards

reacts_against: hustle culture, urban density and digital burnout; cottagecore imagines an unhurried, self-sufficient rural life as an antidote, which is part of why it surged specifically during 2020 lockdowns.
article: Cottagecore sells a specific kind of slowness, and its colors are the proof. The aesthetic took shape on Tumblr around 2018, built from images of English countryside cottages, floral cotton dresses, baking bread and tending gardens — a soft rural fantasy assembled almost entirely from other media (Beatrix Potter illustration, Anne of Green Gables, Studio Ghibli's rural films) rather than from any single real place or era. Its breakout moment came in 2020, when global lockdowns made an unhurried, self-sufficient, nature-close life suddenly feel both impossible and intensely desirable, and cottagecore imagery offered an escape hatch that needed no travel, just a moodboard. The palette draws almost entirely from things that grow or are hand-made: sage and moss green, wheat and buttermilk yellow, dusty rose, terracotta, the warm cream of unbleached linen — nothing neon, nothing fully saturated, because nothing in the source imagery (gardens, baked goods, worn cotton) ever is. It's a close cousin to several aesthetics that split off to cover ground cottagecore's cheerful sunlight didn't reach: witchcore kept the rural palette but pushed the mood toward dusk and ritual, and goblincore kept the muddy, textured naturalism but gave up cottagecore's tidiness for something messier and more amphibian.

wiki_facts.key_colours: Earthy and natural tones (brown, moss green, beige), soft pastels, faded floral prints, gingham
wiki_facts.key_values: Simplicity, self-sufficiency, harmony with nature, domesticity, nostalgia, gentleness, anti-modernism
